origin.description: Apply an ICU transform id or a set of transliteration rules.
origin.usage: stri_trans_general(str, id, rules = FALSE, forward = TRUE)

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A character vector, or an object coerced to character.

arguments.name: id
arguments.text: One transform identifier, such as Latin-ASCII or Any-Hex, or custom rules when rules is TRUE.

arguments.name: rules
arguments.text: TRUE treats id as semicolon-separated transliteration rules.

arguments.name: forward
arguments.text: TRUE runs the transform forward. FALSE runs it in reverse.

origin.details: Transliteration does not depend on the current locale. A missing id makes every result missing. A missing string stays missing. Ids can be chained with a semicolon.
origin.example:
x <- stri_trans_general("groß", "Latin-ASCII")
cat(paste0("stri_trans_general of groß with Latin-ASCII returns ", x, ".\n"))

translation.description: Apply an ICU transform id or a set of transliteration rules.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A character vector, or an object coerced to character.

arguments.name: id
arguments.text: One transform identifier, such as Latin-ASCII or Any-Hex, or custom rules when rules is TRUE.

arguments.name: rules
arguments.text: TRUE treats id as semicolon-separated transliteration rules.

arguments.name: forward
arguments.text: TRUE runs the transform forward. FALSE runs it in reverse.

translation.details: ICU Transliterator.createInstance compiles an id such as Latin-ASCII or Any-Hex. rules True uses createFromRules. forward False requests the inverse direction. A missing id makes every result missing. A missing string stays missing.
translation.value: A string, or NA. A list returns a list. None returns an empty list.
translation.example:
from stringi.trans import stri_trans_general
x = stri_trans_general("groß", "Latin-ASCII")
print(f"stri_trans_general of groß with Latin-ASCII returns {x}.")
